name: Echthge

attributes.attribute: an Irish goddess of the Tuatha Dé Danann
the god of the Silver Hand and father of Echthge
the hills in east Clare named for Echthge
the older hag goddess of the pre-Celtic past whose name marks many local places

sources: Gwynn, Edward. The Metrical Dindshenchas. Vol. III. Royal Irish Academy, Todd Lecture Series. Dublin: Hodges, Figgis, and Co., Ltd., 1906–1924, 201–213.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Echthge is an Irish goddess of the Tuatha Dé Danann. Her land lies in the rolling hills called Slieve Aughty in east county Clare. She was the daughter of Nuada of the Silver Hand. The hills named for her came to her as a dowry after she slept with a paramour. Little is known beyond her titles. Writers call her the awful one and terrible goddess. A stray legend says she ate her own children. Many local names recall the Cailleach, the older hag goddess of the pre-Celtic past. This Echthge may have merged with that older being.

okr.objective: Present Echthge as the Tuatha Dé goddess tied to the Slieve Aughty hills.
key_results: Echthge belongs to the Tuatha Dé Danann, daughter of Nuada of the Silver Hand.
She received the Slieve Aughty hills as a dowry after she slept with a paramour.
Her titles include the awful one and the terrible goddess.
She may have merged with the older Cailleach, pre-Celtic hag goddess, of the region.
